unit: hazard per hour per eligible cell and currently offered action; uncalibrated model parameter, before expression/context multipliers
step_probability: For eligible hazards k_i and multiplier m_i, lambda=sum(k_i*m_i); P(any)=1-exp(-lambda*dt); P(action_i)=P(any)*(k_i*m_i/lambda); REST=exp(-lambda*dt). At most one event per cell per step. A hazard is not a measured cell-cycle rate or an empirical fate probability.
review_status: DRAFT — SCIENTIFIC AUDIT RECORDED; NOT VALIDATED. All numerical hazards remain explicit modelling assumptions; cited primary studies are contextual anchors, not direct calibrations of these generic per-cell transition hazards. Verify applicability to organism, tissue, disease, assay, cell state, spatial contact and time horizon; sensitivity analysis and domain-owner approval remain required before validation/publication.

confidence_levels.assumed: No primary measurement identified that estimates this exact transition hazard for the model's generic lineage/action. Keep the value as a declared assumption and include it in sensitivity analysis.
confidence_levels.contextual_anchor: A verified primary study measures a related phenomenon in a specified experimental system, but does not estimate this generic model parameter; it must not be described as quantitative validation.

ctl_serial_killing.citation: Halle S et al. In Vivo Killing Capacity of Cytotoxic T Cells Is Limited and Involves Dynamic Interactions and T Cell Cooperativity. Immunity. 2016;44(2):233–245.
ctl_serial_killing.summary: Primary intravital study of antiviral CTL interactions in mouse tissue; reports limited killing capacity and cooperation across repeated encounters. Related in-vivo studies span target-killing times of hours, but these include encounter, recognition and target-death dynamics.
ctl_serial_killing.relevance: Context only for cytotoxicity timescale and dependence on repeated cognate encounters.
ctl_serial_killing.limitation: Does not estimate a universal 0.2 h^-1 per-CTL hazard for killing any adjacent malignant cell. Tissue, target, antigen, CTL state, encounter rate and the definition of kill differ. A graph neighbor is not proof of contact or antigen recognition.

ctl_killing_adoptive.citation: Bréart B, Lemaître F, Celli S, Bousso P. Two-photon imaging of intratumoral CD8+ T cell cytotoxic activity during adoptive T cell therapy in mice. J Clin Invest. 2008;118(4):1390–1397.
ctl_killing_adoptive.summary: Primary intravital imaging in a mouse solid-tumour adoptive-transfer model using in-vitro-activated CTLs and apoptosis reporter; measures tumour-cell apoptosis in that treatment context.
ctl_killing_adoptive.relevance: Related tumor-killing context, not a generic kinetic calibration.
ctl_killing_adoptive.limitation: The experimental system is activated adoptively transferred CTLs in a defined mouse tumour; observed apoptosis timing cannot be transferred as a universal single-cell hazard without encounter, target and treatment model.

cd8_expansion.citation: Murali-Krishna K et al. Counting antigen-specific CD8 T cells: a reevaluation of bystander activation during viral infection. Immunity. 1998;8(2):177–187.
cd8_expansion.summary: Primary mouse viral-infection study quantifying antigen-specific CD8 T-cell expansion and the contribution of bystander activation.
cd8_expansion.relevance: Supports antigen-specific clonal expansion as a biological phenomenon.
cd8_expansion.limitation: Population expansion counts do not identify a per-cell exponential PROLIFERATE hazard or a generic division interval.

cd8_cycle_time.citation: Yoon H, Kim TS, Braciale TJ. The cell cycle time of CD8+ T cells responding in vivo is controlled by the type of antigenic stimulus. PLoS One. 2010;5(12):e15423.
cd8_cycle_time.summary: Primary mouse study of naïve antigen-specific CD8 T cells in secondary lymphoid organs; measured initial cell-cycle times that varied by antigen/immunization regimen (including approximately 6 h in a peptide-immunization condition and faster values in selected infection conditions).
cd8_cycle_time.relevance: Shows that measured division timing is stimulus- and protocol-dependent.
cd8_cycle_time.limitation: Does not justify a generic, memoryless per-hour hazard. The reported activated-cell 0.08/h is not a calibrated translation of a measured cycle time, and the model has no implemented timed activation state that applies it.

melanoma_ki67.citation: Gimotty PA et al. Biologic and prognostic significance of dermal Ki67 expression, mitoses, and tumorigenicity in thin invasive cutaneous melanoma. J Clin Oncol. 2005;23(31):8048–8056.
melanoma_ki67.summary: Primary human pathology/prognostic study of thin invasive cutaneous melanoma reporting dermal Ki-67 and mitotic measures.
melanoma_ki67.relevance: Provides a proliferation-associated marker in a particular human melanoma cohort.
melanoma_ki67.limitation: A Ki-67 labeling fraction is not a per-cell division hazard, growth rate or doubling time. Converting it to 0.002–0.008/h by assuming a 2–3 day cycle is an additional unsupported assumption; do not call the resulting rate literature-measured.

exhaustion_timescale.citation: Wherry EJ et al. Viral persistence alters CD8 T-cell immunodominance and tissue distribution and results in distinct stages of functional impairment. J Virol. 2003;77(8):4911–4927.
exhaustion_timescale.summary: Primary mouse LCMV study comparing acute and persistent infection; functional impairment was hierarchical and associated with persistent antigen/viral load.
exhaustion_timescale.relevance: Supports chronic-antigen dependence and staged functional impairment.
exhaustion_timescale.limitation: Does not estimate a constant 0.005/h transition into a generic exhaustion state; transcript markers or a timed-state-free model do not establish functional exhaustion.

epidermal_turnover.citation: Halprin KM. Epidermal 'turnover time'—a re-examination. Br J Dermatol. 1972;86(1):14–19.
epidermal_turnover.summary: Critical review (not a primary experiment) concluding normal epidermal transit from cell formation to surface is likely 40–56 days; psoriatic epidermis is faster.
epidermal_turnover.relevance: Context for epidermal transit, not generic epithelial division.
epidermal_turnover.limitation: Transit time is not basal-cell cycle time or a per-cell PROLIFERATE hazard. It is the wrong quantity to calibrate a generic epithelial lineage.

endothelial_turnover.citation: Hobson B, Denekamp J. Endothelial proliferation in tumours and normal tissues: continuous labelling studies. Br J Cancer. 1984;49(4):405–413.
endothelial_turnover.summary: Primary continuous-labeling study in five mouse tumours and normal tissues: tumour endothelial potential doubling times 2.4–13 days; normal-tissue endothelial turnover estimates 47–23,000 days.
endothelial_turnover.relevance: Demonstrates large context-dependent differences between tumour and normal endothelium.
endothelial_turnover.limitation: Potential doubling time and turnover-time estimates are not interchangeable with a generic per-cell hazard. The current single endothelial value cannot represent both normal and tumour endothelium; 0.001/h should remain assumed pending context-specific calibration.

PROLIFERATE.note: Declared resting-state baseline only; no direct estimate identified. Does not represent an activated-cell cycle time.

ACTIVATE.note: Declared heuristic; antigen, costimulation, priming compartment and activation lag are not represented by this constant rate.

EXHAUST.note: Assumption, not a fitted rate. Wherry et al. support chronic-antigen dependence and staged dysfunction, not a constant transition hazard. Timed states are not implemented.

RECOVER.note: No recovery experiment or explicit recovery-state kinetics calibrates this value.

SECRETE.note: Abstract secretion action; no analyte, secretion amount, duration or per-cell secretion rate is modeled.

APOPTOSIS.note: Generic declared assumption; survival depends on cell state and context, neither calibrated here.

KILL.note: Still an assumed per-eligible-cell hazard. 0.2/h implies a 5 h mean waiting time only under a constant exponential hazard, not an observed universal kill interval. Halle and Bréart are context-specific; the model's recognition gate and spatial neighbor are not equivalent to experimentally verified cognate contact.

EXHAUST.note: The cited contextual study concerns CD8 T cells in chronic LCMV; it does not calibrate CD4 exhaustion.

CLEAR_CORPSE.note: Declared assumption for an eligible neighboring corpse; encounter, recognition and engulfment completion are not separately modeled.

PROLIFERATE.note: Declared quiescent-context heuristic; fibroblast cycling varies strongly with tissue, wound and tumour state.

Contextual primary measurements range from tumour potential doubling times of days to normal endothelial turnover of weeks–years. This single generic value is not calibrated and cannot cover both contexts.
Contextual citation is a review of epidermal transit time, not a primary measurement of generic epithelial cell-cycle hazard; rate is an assumption.

Not inferred from Ki-67. Ki-67 fraction plus an assumed cycle time does not identify this hazard; the implied ln(2)/k doubling time (about 4.8 days ignoring death) is a mathematical model implication, not a measured melanoma doubling time.
